newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble stable ahead of T-bill auctions, quarter-end.
newsitem.headline: Rouble stable ahead of T-bill auctions, quarter-end.

text.p: The rouble was little changed on Tuesday and dealers said its usual gradual decline had stopped as funds were sought for Wednesday's Treasury bill auctions and for squaring balance sheets ahead of the quarter-end.
"Big purchase volumes are likely at tomorrow's T-bill auctions after the recent price fall. This is why rouble/dollar rates are stable," United Investment Bank chief dealer Alexander Suchkov said.
On Wednesday the central bank is auctioning seven trillion roubles of six-month paper and four trillion roubles of four-month bills.
Vozrozhdenye Bank chief dealer Maksim Poltavets said banks could also need roubles to square quarter-end balances and make compulsory reserve payments.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,393-96 per dollar compared with an early 5,391-94 and 5,393-96 late on Monday. Tomorrow roubles edged down to 5,399-5,401 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,395-98.
The central bank said it had set 5,371/5,411 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Tuesday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 50-70 percent compared with Monday's late 10-25 percent.
Dealers forecast the rouble fall was likely to resume after the T-bill auctions and the quarter-end.
